title: Serapeum of Alexandria
source: Ordinary Serapeum column/sphinx photographs and named standard-map constituent point; the site and component QIDs are distinct.
axis: +X east;+Y up;+Z south. Round column is rotationally ambiguous; paired sphinxes face approximately southeast from the inspected view direction.
identityStatus: The candidate is the Serapeum site Q521646. Its reference coordinate is about 88m southeast of the actual named column point. Standard PMTiles monument17593449217372 fixes the component center at29.8963925242424,31.182580653236712; the ordinary OpenStreetMap node1263172956 page confirms Pompei's Pillar and component Q492487. These are deliberately distinct site/component identities. The ordinary site photographs explicitly show this column and paired sphinxes as the Serapeum remains. mappedIdentity records that reviewed constituent association, not an assertion that the node has the site's QID. Native +X east/+Z south, runtime heading0. Approximate southeast-facing sphinx arrangement follows the photographed viewpoint; their spacing and bearing are picture-led estimates, not surveyed plans.

reconstruction.scope: Serapeum of Alexandria surviving landmark group: tall plain tapered granite column, moulded base and leafy Corinthian crown with concave square abacus; two separately based worn sphinxes with frontal heads, nemes flaps, chest/paws and simplified crouching rear masses. Pale restored plinths and original rough stone blocks remain distinct. Keep the surrounding archaeological ground open; no destroyed intact Serapis temple, inferred extensive ruins or hidden galleries are reconstructed.

reconstruction.heightBasis: The three inspected ordinary 2009 photographs guide the approximately27m column, slender unfluted entasis, flared leafy capital/concave abacus, square/moulded foot, worn frontal sphinx heads and long nemes flaps, paired paws, rough original blocks and pale tapered restored plinths. Shaft diameter about2.6m and sphinx/plinth height about4m are picture-led estimates. Sphinx back/animal anatomy, individual leaves/volutes, damaged facial carving and exact ancient inscriptions are simplified; no measured conservation record is claimed.
reconstruction.terrainBasis: Pinned standard Protomaps2026-10-14 and Mapzen13–14 extract, recentered on the named column point. Retain its original six-meter native grid and water. Column and each sphinx have separate locally sampled level footings with buried bottoms; no continuous fabricated podium spans the precinct. The coarse DEM does not resolve excavation walls or exact restored paving levels. Local foot/plinth heights, spacing and contact are approximate; surrounding low ruins and visitor landscape remain host context. No terrain, water or building cutout.
